# The bounded Mahler measures inside a field generated by a small unit

<a id="statement"></a>
## High-degree elements lie in one group of units

Let \(K=\mathbb Q(x)\) have degree \(d\), where \(x\) is a nontorsion algebraic unit such that every positive power generates \(K\).
There is a unit \(\epsilon\in K\) such that, for \(y\in K^\times\) of infinite multiplicative order,
\[
     y\text{ is multiplicatively dependent with }x
       \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
     y=\xi\epsilon^k\quad(\xi\in\mu(K),\ k\in\mathbb Z\setminus\{0\}).
                                                                            \tag{1}
\]
Here \(\mu(K)\) is the finite group of roots of unity in \(K\).
Every element on the right and every one of its positive powers generates \(K\); its total logarithmic measure is \(|k|m(\epsilon)\).
Moreover \(m(\epsilon)=m(x)/s\) for an integer \(s\ge1\).
At fixed \(M\ge m(x)\), there is an absolute constant \(C\) such that every nontorsion \(y\in K\) with \(m(y)\le M\) and
\[
                 [\mathbb Q(y):\mathbb Q]>
                         C M m(\epsilon)(\log(3d))^{212}                  \tag{2}
\]
satisfies (1).
In particular, if \(d\) exceeds the threshold in (2), the distinct positive measures at most \(M\) occurring above that threshold are exactly
\[
                  m(\epsilon),\,2m(\epsilon),\ldots,\,
                    \lfloor M/m(\epsilon)\rfloor\,m(\epsilon).
\]
They occur at degree \(d\), and none occurs at an intermediate degree above the threshold and below \(d\).
The same numerical values might also occur at degrees at or below the threshold.

<a id="primitive"></a>
## Saturation inside the original unit group

A relation \(y^b=\xi x^a\) for integers \(b>0,\ a\ne0\) and torsion \(\xi\) forces \(y\) to be a unit at every finite place.
Dirichlet's unit theorem gives \(\mathcal O_K^\times/\mu(K)\) as a finitely generated free abelian group.
In any lattice basis divide the nonzero vector of \(x\) by the greatest common divisor \(s\) of its coordinates.
The resulting primitive vector generates the intersection of its rational line with the lattice by Bézout's identity; take a unit representative \(\epsilon\).
This proves (1) and gives \(x=\omega\epsilon^s\) with \(\omega\in\mu(K)\).
For \(y=\xi\epsilon^k\) with \(k\ne0\) and any integer \(j\ge1\), raising \(y^j\) to \(s|\mu(K)|\) gives \(x^{kj|\mu(K)|}\), a generator of \(K\).
Negative powers generate the same field as their inverses.
Thus all claimed fields equal \(K\), and the degree-times-height formula gives the exact measures.
For any \(y\) off this line the [independent height product at joint degree \(d\)](Yin_C_G0901_v42.md#independent) gives
\[
                   m(\epsilon)m(y)\gg
                       \frac{[\mathbb Q(y):\mathbb Q]}{(\log(3d))^{212}} .
\]
This proves (2) and the spectrum statement.

<a id="trace"></a>
## Every nontorsion generator of the trace field has large total measure

Suppose in addition \(x\) is reciprocal and write \(K^+=\mathbb Q(x+x^{-1})\).
This is the fixed field of the nontrivial inverter \(\tau\) and has degree \(d/2\), with no total-reality assumption.
Every nontorsion \(y\in (K^+)^\times\) is off the line in (1), as the elements on that line generate \(K\).
Therefore every nontorsion generator of the trace field satisfies
\[
                        m(y)\gg\frac{d}{m(\epsilon)(\log(3d))^{212}}.     \tag{3}
\]
In particular a hypothetical sequence of such generators with the original \(m(x)\to0\) and \(d\to\infty\) forces the right side of (3) to diverge.
This applies to every nontorsion generator, integral or otherwise, even when all embeddings of the trace field are nonreal.
For an arbitrary proper subfield \(H\subsetneq K\), its relative norm \(u=N_{K/H}(\epsilon)\) has \(m(u)\le m(\epsilon)\) by the height inequality for a product and \([\mathbb Q(u):\mathbb Q]\le[H:\mathbb Q]\).
Hence either \(u\) is torsion or \([\mathbb Q(u):\mathbb Q]\ll m(\epsilon)^2(\log(3d))^{212}\).

<a id="selection"></a>
## Application to the unrestricted infimum

If the unrestricted infimum of positive Mahler measures vanishes, choose nontorsion unit minima with total measures tending to zero by the [small-measure reduction](Yin_C_G0345_v408.md#lower).
The [relative norm preserving total measure](Yin_C_G0345_v421.md#norm) gives representatives \(x\) all of whose positive powers generate their fields.
For these inputs the above \(\epsilon\) still generates the same field in every positive power.
Its positive measure is at most \(m(x)\), and its degree must tend to infinity by bounded-degree finiteness.
At sufficiently small measure [Smyth's bound](../audits/literature/Smy71/Yin_U001.md#smy71-statement-and-conventions) gives reciprocity of both \(x\) and \(\epsilon\).
Their inverters on \(K\) agree since they invert the same generator \(x^{|\mu(K)|}=\epsilon^{s|\mu(K)|}\).
The unrestricted zero alternative therefore already admits primitive generators as in (1) with the full trace-field and internal-spectrum restrictions above.
The converse follows because these generators are themselves unrestricted integer-polynomial inputs.
